real_qa.q: Why did Grill Nation rebrand from Entrepreneur KC, and what was the trigger for the timing of this change?
real_qa.r: Jason Grill felt it was the right time because he had been advised to put his name in the show. The show had evolved beyond just entrepreneurs and startups—after three years and conducting 400 to 500 interviews, it was covering newsmakers, thought leaders, politicians, business icons, CEOs of major companies, lawyers, financial experts, and entertainers. The rebrand reflected that the show had become much more than just about Kansas City entrepreneurs.

real_qa.q: What expansion plans does Grill Nation have beyond the studio to grow its reach?
real_qa.r: Jason Grill plans to do remote broadcasts from major Kansas City events and national events, including potential shows in different cities. He specifically mentioned attending South By in Austin to interview guests and do remote segments. real_qa.q: What is Houndstooth's location and business model in Kansas City's River Market?
real_qa.r: Houndstooth is located at 507 Walnut Street in the River Market and operates as a men's clothing and tailoring shop. It offers high-end menswear including shoes, shirts, and sports coats, alongside local goods. The shop also functions as an event space for parties and gatherings. Jeff Kovitz, the owner, chose the River Market specifically because he believes it represents the densest urban area in downtown Kansas City with strong neighborhood characteristics.
real_qa.requete: Houndstooth River Market Kansas City location

real_qa.q: What is the distinction between style and trend in men's fashion according to Houndstooth's philosophy?
real_qa.r: According to Jeff Kovitz, style endures while fashion and trends come and go. Adult men should not strive to be trendy but rather develop style, which is more attainable and looks better through the years. Trends pass quickly, whereas style is demonstrated by figures like Steve McQueen, whose vintage looks still appear great today, unlike trendy clothing that may look outdated in a few years.
real_qa.requete: style versus trend men's fashion philosophy

real_qa.q: What family heritage and business background influenced Jeff Kovitz's decision to open Houndstooth?
real_qa.r: Jeff Kovitz's grandfather owned Leo's Tailor Shop in Brookside from 1952 to 2000—nearly 50 years in business. Jeff's father, Rick, continued the tailoring tradition, and Jeff worked for his father his whole life, starting to work full-time with him around age 23. After his father passed away, Jeff took over Rick's Tailoring for four years before deciding to focus entirely on Houndstooth in the River Market.
